intro: Body parts and accidents: «me he roto el brazo», «me caí», «me corté un dedo».
p.romperse.consejo: The participle is irregular: «roto». You say «me he roto el brazo», with «me».
p.caerse.consejo: It is irregular: «me caigo» in the present and «me caí» in the past. It takes «se»: «se cayó».
p.cortarse.consejo: You say «me corté el dedo»: the body part takes «el», not «mi».
p.torcerse.consejo: It is irregular: «me tuerzo» in the present, but «me torcí» in the past. You twist an ankle.
p.darse un golpe.consejo: You say «me di un golpe en la cabeza». The form «di» has no accent.
p.doler.consejo: It works like «gustar»: «me duele el brazo», «me duelen los pies». It changes o to ue.
p.brazo.consejo: It is masculine: «el brazo». With «me» and a body part you use the article, not «mi».
p.codo.consejo: You say «me di un golpe en el codo». The c sounds k before o: KO-do.
p.tobillo.consejo: The ll sounds like y: to-BI-yo. It is what you twist when running: «me torcí el tobillo».
p.herida.consejo: The h is silent: e-RI-da. It comes from «herir».
p.tirita.consejo: In Spain you say «tirita»; in Latin America «curita» is also used.
p.escayola.consejo: The y sounds as in «yo»: es-ka-YO-la. It is put on so that the broken bone does not move.
p.venda.consejo: The v sounds like b: BEN-da. Do not mix it up with «venta», which is selling.
p.hielo.consejo: The h is silent and «hie» is read «ye»: YE-lo. After a bump it is put on the sore area.
b1.texto:
To tell about an accident we use a verb with **me**, **te**, **se**… and the body part with an article, not with «mi»:

- **Me he roto** el brazo.
- **Me corté** el dedo cocinando.
- **Me torcí** el tobillo.
- **Me di** un golpe en la cabeza.

The pronoun already says whose arm it is, so we do not say «mi brazo».

To ask: **¿Qué te ha pasado?**, **¿Te duele?**

To treat it: a **tirita** (small wound), a **venda**, **hielo** or an **escayola** (broken bone).
b2.f2.texto: I was on my bike, I fell and I banged my elbow.
b2.f3.texto: Did they put a cast on you?
b2.f4.texto: They put it on this morning.
b2.f7.texto: It only hurts when I move my hand.
b2.f8.texto: Yesterday I cut my finger and only needed a plaster.
b4.texto:
The body part takes **el / la** and the pronoun says whose it is:

- **Me** he roto **el** brazo. (not «mi brazo»)
- **Se** ha cortado **la** mano.

To tell the accident, three tenses combine:

- **Imperfect** for the scene: **iba** en bici, **estaba** cocinando.
- **Preterite** for what happens suddenly: **me caí**, **me corté**.
- **Present perfect** if it is recent: **me he roto** el brazo.
b4.e1.texto: I was cooking when I cut my finger.
b4.e2.texto: My sister has cut her hand.
b5.f0.texto: Pablo rides down the slope on his bike with the wind in his face.
b5.f1.texto: The wheels hum over the dry dirt track.
b5.f2.texto: A big stone suddenly appears in front of the wheel.
b5.f3.texto: Pablo brakes too late and loses his balance.
b5.f4.texto: The ground rises to meet him with a dull thud.
b5.f5.texto: Pablo hears nothing for a few seconds.
b5.f6.texto: Then he feels a hot pain in his elbow and his wrist.
b5.f7.texto: A neighbour runs towards him with a bottle of cold water.
b5.f8.texto: The neighbour cleans his wound very carefully and puts a white bandage on him.
b5.f9.texto: Pablo clenches his teeth and smiles despite the pain.
b6.o0.refuerzo: That's it! With «me» we already know whose it is: the article is used.
b6.o1.refuerzo: With «me» you do not use «mi»: the pronoun already says whose it is.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Brazo» is masculine: it cannot go with «la».
b6.pregunta: It already says «me». Which word goes before «brazo»?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Well done! A plaster is enough for a small cut.
b7.o1.refuerzo: A cast is for a broken bone, not for a cut.
b7.o2.refuerzo: The ankle is a body part, not something you put on.
b7.pregunta: You have a small cut on your finger. What do you put on?
b8.frase: Me di un golpe en la cabeza
b9.o0.refuerzo: «Cayó» is for «él» or «ella». Here the speaker is «yo».
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Caigo» is present, but the sentence is about yesterday.
b9.o2.refuerzo: That's it! «Caí» is «yo» in the past: ayer me caí.
b9.pregunta: It is «yo» and the past. Which form is missing?
b10.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I sprained my ankle.»
b11.o0.refuerzo: That asks whether he fell, not whether it hurts.
b11.o1.refuerzo: Well done! «¿Te duele?» asks about the pain.
b11.o2.refuerzo: That asks what happened, not whether there is pain now.
b11.pregunta: You want to know whether it hurts. What do you ask?
b12.frase: Estaba cocinando cuando me ____ un dedo.
b12.o0.refuerzo: The imperfect describes the scene; the cut was a quick moment.
b12.o1.refuerzo: That's it! Preterite for what happens suddenly: me corté.
b12.o2.refuerzo: The infinitive does not work here: a conjugated form is needed.
b12.pregunta: A quick moment interrupts the scene. Which form is missing?
p.pasado.consejo: Participle of «pasar». «¿Qué te ha pasado?» means what happened to you?
p.roto.consejo: Irregular participle of «romper». The initial r is strong: RRO-to. Not «rompido».
p.bici.consejo: Short for «bicicleta». The c before i sounds th: BI-thi. It is feminine: «la bici».
p.caí.consejo: Past form of «caer» for «yo». The accent splits a-í into two syllables: ka-Í.
p.torcí.consejo: Past form of «torcer» for «yo»: «me torcí el tobillo». The c sounds th before i.
p.muevo.consejo: Form of «mover»: the o becomes «ue». The v sounds like b: MWE-bo.
p.corté.consejo: Past form of «cortar» for «yo». The accent shows the stress: kor-TÉ.
p.dedo.consejo: The d is soft: DE-do. It is masculine: «el dedo». The toes are «los dedos del pie».
p.necesité.consejo: Past form of «necesitar» for «yo». The c before e sounds th and the accent is last: ne-the-si-TÉ.
p.cocinando.consejo: Gerund of «cocinar». «Estaba cocinando» describes an action in progress in the past.
p.cortado.consejo: Participle of «cortar». With «haber» it does not change: «se ha cortado la mano».
p.bicicleta.consejo: The c before i sounds th: bi-thi-KLE-ta. The short form is «la bici».
p.ruedas.consejo: The initial r is strong: RRWE-das. The singular is «la rueda».
p.zumban.consejo: The z sounds th: THUM-ban. The noun is «el zumbido», the sound of a bee.
p.seca.consejo: Feminine of «seco». The c before a sounds k: SE-ka. It agrees with «tierra».
p.piedra.consejo: The «ie» is one syllable: PYE-dra. It is feminine: «una piedra».
p.frena.consejo: Form of «frenar», from «el freno», the brake.
p.pierde.consejo: Form of «perder»: the e becomes «ie». «Perder el equilibrio» means to lose your balance.
p.encuentro.consejo: «Ir al encuentro» means to go to meet someone or something. It comes from «encontrar».
p.dolor.consejo: The stress is at the end: do-LOR. It is masculine: «el dolor». The verb is «doler».
p.aprieta.consejo: Form of «apretar»: the e becomes «ie». «Apretar los dientes» means to clench your teeth.
p.pesar.consejo: Here it is part of «a pesar de», despite. The stress is at the end: pe-SAR.
